identity: A page from a children's magazine. The first three lines are masthead furniture, not story text: the standing column name النافذة المفتوحة (The Open Window); a weekly credits line naming the writer محمد أبو قمر and the illustrator نبيل تاج; and then the story title الكلب المغرور والعين السحرية. Everything after that is a moral fable for children in literary MSA: past-tense narrative, unmarked direct speech introduced by قال/يقول with no quotation marks, relentless و-coordination, and staccato rhetorical repetition. The conceited dog Lucky boasts, runs off to the forest, cowers from the elephant, kills the wise rabbit Arnoub, drinks from the enchanted spring, swells into a monster, is laughed at because his leash still dangles, shrinks back, and is dragged home by his owner.
law: The unit is the narrative beat: one event or one speech act plus everything و-chained to it - same-subject verb runs, adverbials, and subordinate clauses with حتى / إذ / بينما / لما / حين / الذي, plus the correlative وإنما. Boundaries come from four sources. (1) MANDATORY: the token before every <NL> and the final token. (2) ASYNDETON - a new independent clause opening with no connective at all: a bare past verb (اختبأ, قال, التفت, تعجبت), a bare كان/ظل/أصبح, a bare adverb (فجأة, حينئذ), or a bare nominal clause (له يدان). This author coordinates everything, so a missing و is his period. Highest confidence. (3) QUOTE CLOSE - unmarked direct speech has to carry its own terminal mark, so the last token of a quote ends the sentence whenever narration resumes after it, even when the resumption begins with و or ثم. (4) DISCOURSE PIVOTS that are sentence-initial in MSA: bare لكن(ه), غير أن, أما...ف, ومع ذلك, وأخيرا, وفعلا, وليس ذلك فحسب. NOT boundaries: ف and ثم as plain coordinators between narrative clauses; asyndetic repetition of the same word (ينبح ينبح, يكبر يكبر); serial predicates sharing one كان (يكبر يزداد طولا يتضخم); any subordinator. Medium-confidence extension: و opening a NEW TABLEAU counts - و + كان starting a fresh description or introducing a new character, و + verb carrying a heavy أن/بأن complement, or و + a re-stated explicit subject, since this author names his subject once per sentence and drops it thereafter.
reasoning: HEADER (i10 قمر): left unmarked. A magazine credits line separates writer from illustrator with a dash, bullet or colon - not a terminal mark - and both names sit on one physical line rather than on separate <NL> lines. || REPEATED أنا-BOASTS (36 أنا جميل | أنا قوي وعظيم; 176 أنا أقوى الأقوياء | أنا عظيم العظماء; 662 أنا جبار | أنا متوحش وهائل): I did NOT split any of the three. Each is one boast in two beats on the same أنا frame, and this author demonstrably uses asyndetic repetition as an internal ellipsis (ينبح ينبح at 956, يكبر يكبر at 621, يصغر يصغر at 965). I DID split 200 (أنا قائد الحيوانات كلها | يجب أن يحترمني الأسد), because that is a shift from self-description to a demand - a different speech act carrying its own long predication. These four sites move together: if grading says the أنا-pairs are boundaries, the whole class flips, and that is the first thing my doctrine should record. || ثم: treated as a plain coordinator and skipped at 216 (هكذا قال الكلب لاكي ثم انطلق), 579 (وابتلعه ثم دس) and 859 (inside a quote) - EXCEPT where the preceding token closes a direct quote (39, 391, 819), where the quote's own terminal mark ends the sentence no matter what follows. || ف: always clause-internal (skipped 60 فهو, 849 فقال في نفسه, 786 فلماذا). Decisive internal evidence: at 382 the author writes the same verb BARE - قال لاكي في نفسه - which is a clear asyndetic boundary, while at 850 he writes فقال. He marks the difference himself, so ف means continue. || وإنما is correlative, never a boundary: skipped 893 after the لم يكن chain, matching its clause-internal use at 79 (ليس لها أصحاب وإنما تنطلق) and 115. I marked 111 instead, before the pivot وليس ذلك فحسب. || LONG و-CHAINS: tight same-subject action runs stay whole (520-534 غضب ... وهاج وأخذ ينبح ويهدده; 535-560 لم يخف وتقدم ودفعه وقال له), but I split و-verbs that each carry a heavy complement and mark a distinct discovery: 909 وفوجئ بأن, 921 واكتشف أن, 989 وأدرك لاكي أن. Without those, paragraph 17 (872-944) would be a single 73-token sentence. At 989 the re-mention of لاكي as explicit subject after two subject-less verbs is the extra evidence; at 981 (وتذكر) there is no re-mention, so I kept it attached to ووقف. || PARAGRAPH 9 (400-447): read as four descriptive strokes rather than one 48-token period - 408 (وحين + new subject لاكي), 422 (وكانت العين تفيض, narratorial description standing outside the اكتشف أن clause), 435 (وكان يقوم على حراسة ... أرنب عجوز, which introduces a new character). All three rest on the medium-confidence new-tableau rule and would fall together if that rule is wrong. || 794 (خادما): the interrogative فلماذا لا تأتي لتعمل في بيتي الجديد خادما has to close with a question mark before the declarative وسوف أجعل زوجي, so I broke there but not at 786, where ف links the statement to the question. || WEAKEST CALLS, both marked lo: 491 (ومع ذلك) reads equally well as a comma inside the غير أن sentence; 714 (وغمز الذئب) is و + a new actor inside one comic tableau, marked only for consistency with 751 (وأخذ الفيل). || DELIBERATELY LEFT LONG: 55-94 (40 tokens) and 271-314 (44 tokens). Each is one periodic structure - a topic sentence plus its التي/إذ explanation, and a reaction chain plus its إذ عرف أنه clause - with no asyndeton anywhere inside, so my law gives them nothing to break on. || Result: 67 boundaries over 1050 non-<NL> tokens, about 15.7 tokens per sentence, which fits children's narrative MSA.
